model.costScope: Augmented recipient expense envelope: 2024 gross operating expense plus netted fiduciary fees and judgmental external medication/nursing allowances. Not a measured complete resource cost or a verified marginal cash-gift price. External medication allowance may overlap recognized prescription/supply expense; no arbitrary subtraction is made without reconciliation.
model.geographicAttribution: Medical Monmouth residency criterion supports g=1 for the modeled medical cohort; sensitivity g=.95 allows leakage. Proposed dental service and state grant areas Monmouth/Ocean are within the official 22-county NYC MSA. Service eligibility is not a measured match of every beneficiary address.
model.formula: C=C0+I+M*w+H*s*k+Cd; N=(D/share)*f; v=rho+ln(1+d); A=(1-exp(-v*T))/v; Qmedical=N*a*b*(p*u*A-h); Qdental=Nd*rd*ad*b*(pd*ud*Td-hd)*od; Qall=Qmedical+Qdental; QMSA=g*Qall; price10=10*C/QMSA if positive, otherwise null. Dental term is scenario-only, half-year undiscounted approximation; it is not included in central.
model.counterfactual: Existing clinic operations, accumulated reserves, appropriated public/private funding, free medicines, other safety-net care and volunteer supply continue. a reflects treatment substituted from alternatives; b is the unknown proportional output response to new unrestricted funding beyond that baseline. Keeping b=.25 is an explicit prior, not inferred from a funding request or asset ratio; 0,.1,.15 and .5 sensitivities expose this uncertainty.
model.attribution: One inferred medical cohort, with aggregate net clinical response, prevents additive counting of overlapping chronic disease, mental health, nutrition and screenings. Central dental and policy gains are unpriced, not proven zero; prospective dental scenario applies additionality and residual-overlap factors and adds an illustrative annual resource allowance.
model.uncertainty: A deeper evidence review, not evidence of causal health effectiveness. Prices are conditional estimates without a calibrated posterior or confidence interval. Current marginal medical and dental output/cost curves are missing; financial solvency does not prove funding irrelevance, and an opening does not prove new gifts caused it. Sources attached to judgment inputs provide context only, not estimates of the numerical coefficients. High two-year gains assume persistence after one funded year; high-recurring-cost explicitly charges a second identical annual envelope.
model.nativeOutcomes: Inferred 1,368 medical people become 171 additional clinical-access equivalents under a=.5 and b=.25; 42.75 modeled responders receive finite utility gain. These are conditional equivalents, not measured successes. Central QALYs are 3.147996.

scenarios.interpretation: Replaces broad response prior; a=.5 denotes combined clinic transfer/additionality. Prevalence difference is not clinical responder probability. Utility and persistence remain unvalidated priors. Do not add to central.

scenarios.label: Optimistic two-year benefit with two annual resource envelopes
scenarios.interpretation: Undiscounted second identical annual cost is a conservative accounting sensitivity, not a forecast of actual year2 spending. No duplicate cohort benefit.

missingInputs: Verified unique annual patients and overlapping medical/dental cohorts.
Parker-controlled comparative clinical outcomes and benefit persistence.
Current 2026 unrestricted operating budget, cash commitments and residual funding gap beyond awarded grants.
Reconciliation of in-kind categories, medication opportunity cost and nursing hours.
Actual dental throughput, dental resource cost including donated space/clinical labor, baseline pain and waiting-time counterfactual.
Full-portfolio long-term prevention, policy, educational benefits and potential harms.
sensitivity: Funding-response b is unmeasured: central .25, .1 and .15 sensitivities are not posterior probabilities.
Central price changes only through restoration of $22,722 investment fees; previous clinical priors retained.
Prospective dental scenario adds an illustrative resource allowance and discounts planned reach, substitution, response and overlap; no actual dental causal claim.
Zero funding response has no finite positive-benefit price; adverse treatment-burden scenario can be negative.
model.nativeCosts: Augmented recipient annual expense envelope $2,427,658 / 1,368 inferred patients = $1,774.60 per inferred patient; $14,196.83 per additional clinical-access equivalent and $56,787.32 per modeled responder. These are accounting-model ratios, not clinic prices or donation quotes.
